examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Keep an invariant describing the interval that can still contain the target, and ensure every binary-search update shrinks it. A bitonic array permits peak location plus two monotonic searches in logarithmic time. A property quantified over all index pairs can sometimes be checked using adjacent comparisons.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A sorted array has 31 distinct keys. Standard middle-key binary search needs at most how many probes for a successful search?

**Answer: 5.** A balanced search tree with 31 keys has five levels: 1+2+4+8+16=31. A deepest key is probed on the fifth comparison, giving maximum 5.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
State whether one comparison means one key probe or separate equality/less-than tests; exact comparison counts depend on that convention.

Binary search over an unsorted array has no correctness guarantee.
